title: aftergrid Analysis file
description: analysis.yaml: the working record of one Analysis, beside manifest.yaml in a Finding directory. Contract: docs/contracts/analysis-directory.md. It lives under src/ rather than schema/ because schema/ holds the artifacts a Reader-facing Finding is validated against; this one is an Engine-internal working record the writer consumes.

stage.description: How far this file has been filled in. `clarified` is the seed /grill-question writes: reader_profile, assumptions, pre_registered_comparison and needs_input, with no evidence recorded yet — a complete artifact for that stage, not a defective one. `analysed` is the working record /checked-analysis leaves once the run has happened, and it requires probes, execution_order, candidate_claims and outcome_recommendation. Absent means `analysed`, so a file written before this field existed keeps its meaning.

clarified_at.description: When the Question was settled: the moment `/grill-question` (or the shared clarification procedure `/analyze` and `/checked-analysis` follow) wrote `question.state: resolved` into the manifest, read from the harness's clock then. It is what makes 'clarify before capture' checkable rather than advice: `analysisWarnings` reports `capture_before_clarify` for any `manifest.snapshot.inputs[].captured_at` earlier than this. Absent means only that the moment was not recorded — `pre_registered_comparison.registered_at` is read instead, and with neither, nothing is claimed either way.

reader_profile.description: The Reader profile id this Analysis is aimed at, from the Instance's readers.md. `generic` when the Instance names none.

assumptions.description: Every choice the Analysis made that the Question did not settle. An empty list asserts that nothing was assumed.

basis.description: Where the assumption came from. `unverified` is honest and allowed; writing it down never upgrades it.

settled_by.description: Who or what settled it: a person, a document path, a probe id.

pre_registered_comparison.description: The primary comparison, written down before any cut was explored. Required for an `answered` recommendation.

registered_before_cuts.description: false is a legitimate, reportable state: the comparison was settled after exploration, and every Claim resting on it is exploratory.

source.description: Where it was registered: the Question in manifest.yaml, a clarification round, an experiment plan.

probes.description: The middle of the analysis, recorded in place: every look at the catalog or the data taken before the plan was committed, every post-hoc look taken after a result was seen, every dead end and every reframe, each with the time it happened. A dead end is recorded, never deleted. Always exploratory; never evidence for a Claim. Entries are kept in non-decreasing `at` order so the list reads as a timeline (`analysisWarnings` warns when they are not).

at.description: When the probe was taken, RFC 3339 with an offset, read from the harness's clock at the time. Never a time invented afterwards to make the list look orderly: a probe whose time is unknown is a probe that was not recorded when it happened, and saying so in `observed` is the honest move.

kind.description: What this look was. `exploratory`: a look that informed the plan. `dead_end`: a path tried or considered and abandoned, kept so the middle of the analysis is visible afterwards. `reframe`: a look that changed the Question itself, which must then say what changed in `changed_plan`.

question.description: What the probe was trying to find out.

observed.description: What it actually showed, in plain words.

sql_path.description: A retained probe query. A probe that was not retained omits this.

changed_plan.description: What the plan did because of it. Required on a `reframe`, where it names the Question change and the `/grill-question` revisit if one happened; a `dead_end` uses it to say what was done instead.

checks_preregistered.description:
Each Check as it stood when it was written, before any analysis query ran. Optional as a list; where an entry exists it is the only mechanical evidence a reviewer has that a Check — above all a falsifier — was not loosened, un-required, re-aimed or rewritten after its result was seen.

What an entry covers, and `check` compares each against the manifest Check, reporting `analysis_contract` on a difference: (1) `content_hash`, the sha256 of the Check's SQL file at that moment; (2) `required`, the evidence-validity flag, so un-requiring a Check afterwards leaves a trace; (3) `expected_outcome`, the verdict the Check had to produce, which lives in manifest.checks and not in the SQL, so flipping it after the result is otherwise invisible; (4) `statement_hash`, the sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes of manifest.question.falsifier.statement, required on the entry for the Check the Question names as its falsifier, so the plain-language bar cannot be restated around the number that came back. A falsifier's entry must carry `expected_outcome`; the Question's falsifier must also carry `statement_hash`.

What it does NOT cover: anything not listed above — the Check's `description`, its `execution_id`, the Question's wording outside `falsifier.statement`, and any Check with no entry here. Absent entirely, the reviewer falls back to the probe/execution_order timeline, which shows the order the files were written and not their content.

The repair for any difference is to say what changed and why, as a `reframe` probe. Re-pinning the recorded value to match the file is never the repair.

content_hash.description: The sha256 of the Check's SQL file at the moment it was written.

at.description: When the Check file was written, read from the harness's clock. Never a time invented afterwards.

required.description: The Check's `required` flag as it was pre-registered. A falsifier is never `required: true` (docs/contracts/checks-and-results.md), so recording `false` here is what makes a later `true` — or a later un-requiring of an invariant — visible.

expected_outcome.description: The outcome the Check had to produce for the Answer to stand, as pre-registered. Required on a `kind: falsifier` Check, because this field lives in manifest.checks rather than in the SQL file and is the cheapest thing to flip after the result is known.

statement_hash.description: sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes of manifest.question.falsifier.statement, as pre-registered. Required on the entry for the Check the Question names as its falsifier.

execution_order.description: Every probe, Check and analysis query in the order it was written and run. Grouped probe -> check -> query; a Check recorded after an analysis query is an error. A probe taken after a query is recorded where it happened, with `post_hoc: true`.

exploratory.description: A query cut that was not pre-registered. Its Claims carry comparison.pre_registered false.

post_hoc.description: Only on a probe: this look was taken after a result was already seen. It is exempt from the probe -> check -> query grouping because hiding it would be the dishonest option, and everything it informs is exploratory.

candidate_claims.description: Draft Claims for the writer. The writer sharpens the sentence; it never changes the evidence, comparison, population, window or type.

causal_basis.description: The design that earns a causal Claim. Required when type is causal, where the only value the validator accepts is randomised_assignment; `none` on a causal Claim is refused and the Claim is associational.

definition_refs.description: Every definition this Claim's numbers rest on, at the version that was read. Each must appear in manifest.definitions at the same version, so a Diagnostic grouping a Claim displays is traced rather than assumed.

kind.description: The same enum as claims[].comparison.kind in schema/finding-manifest.schema.json: the writer copies this value through unchanged, so the two lists cannot disagree.

material_caveat.description: Required on the answer-bearing Claim: the caveat that would change the conclusion.

recheck_draft.description: The Recheck policy in draft. `not_automatically_evaluable` with a reason and an owner is a complete answer, not a gap.

predicate.description: The proposition in words: subject, operator, threshold, unit, direction.

requested_derived.description: Derived values a candidate Claim needs and the writer will declare in manifest.derived. The Analysis names the operation and the operands; it does not compute the number. Candidate evidence may cite these ids as `derived:<id>` before manifest.derived exists.

requested_external_sources.description: Typed values that do not come from a query — a target, an assumption, an external reference — which a candidate Claim needs and the writer will declare in manifest.external_sources. Candidate evidence may cite these ids as `ext:<id>` before manifest.external_sources exists.

outcome_recommendation.description: What the Analysis concluded. The writer records it as finding.outcome; it never upgrades it.

what_would_be_needed.description: For a non-answer: what would have to be true before the Question can be answered. Required for every outcome except `answered` — it is what makes a non-answer usable.

needs_input.description: What the Analysis stopped for. Each item is specific enough that the named owner can act without asking back.

unit.description: The same enum as $defs/unit in schema/finding-manifest.schema.json: a business unit, never inferred from a SQL type.
